item.title: Digital attention disruption and academic impact in adolescents: a data-driven network and machine learning analysis
item.description: Academic impact associated with digital media use is a topic of considerable concern in the fields of adolescent mental health and education; however, the role of attention status in this context remains largely unknown.

item.title: Algorithmic management and gig workers' workplace wellbeing: the moderating role of psychological resilience
item.description: We find that algorithmic management is positively associated with both challenge appraisal and threat appraisal. Challenge appraisal is positively associated with workplace wellbeing, whereas threat appraisal is negatively associated with workplace wellbeing.

item.title: The post-necessary human: artificial intelligence, societal security, and cognitive governance
item.description: The post-necessary human is introduced as an analytical construct describing a relational condition in which AI-mediated systems simultaneously reduce human functional necessity and displace human agency within specific domains of activity.

item.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Cognitive Scaffolding, Substitution, and the Risk of Deskilling
item.description: Evidence from recent empirical studies suggests a dual pattern: structured forms of AI assistance can sustain users’ cognitive activity and enhance engagement and performance, whereas more substitutive forms of use are associated with reduced autonomous reasoning and poorer subsequent independent performance.

item.title: Disrupted network reconfiguration during task switching in insomnia: the role of sleep-related attentional bias
item.description: The ID group exhibited significantly lower CFI scores compared to the HC group, indicating subjective cognitive flexibility impairment. These findings suggest that insomnia is characterized by both subjective deficits in cognitive flexibility and altered neural network dynamics during task switching, with sleep-related stimuli exerting a significant modulatory effect.

item.title: Parental Notification Gaps in ChatGPT-5: An Empirical Study
item.description: We evaluate how effectively platform-level parental controls moderate a mainstream conversational assistant used by minors.

item.title: Freirean Pedagogy for Equitable Assessment, Decolonial Governance, and Cognitive Wellbeing in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review
item.description: Paulo Freire’s critical pedagogy offers a powerful lens for interrogating the epistemological, ethical, and political dimensions of AI-mediated education, yet its application remains fragmented across disciplinary boundaries. Key findings reveal that uncritical AI integration reproduces the banking model of education, systematically marginalizes nondominant epistemologies, and risks eroding critical thinking through cognitive debt.

item.title: AI in education: boosting productivity or challenging cognitive effort?
item.description: Although AI is associated with greater time efficiency and improved academic performance, its broader effects on student productivity and cognitive effort remain insufficiently understood. Self-confidence appears to be associated with likelihood to reap significant rather than some productivity gains particularly once the interaction of AI dependency and AI-led cognitive shift is accounted for.

item.title: AI-MEDIATED WELLBEING SURVEILLANCE AND THE BOUNDARY OF PSYCHOLOGICAL SAFETY
item.description: This paper develops a conceptual model of how AI-mediated wellbeing monitoring reshapes psychological safety, the shared belief that a work environment is safe for interpersonal risk-taking on which voice, dissent and error reporting depend.

item.title: Recommendation in the era of GenAI: from an attention economy to a trust economy
item.description: The article examines the shift in the digital cultural ecosystem triggered by the widespread adoption of Generative AI. Ultimately, this paper argues that platforms transition from a pure attention economy to a trust economy, actively protecting and highlighting human-made works to preserve the integrity and sustainability of the cultural value chain.

item.title: Between Human and Machine: University Teachers’ Accounts of Judgment, Metacognitive Defense, and Cognitive Offloading in Generative AI Use
item.description: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) allows university teachers to delegate cognitive work while deciding how students should engage with it. Using codebook thematic analysis, we examined multi-source accounts from 25 teachers recruited through an AI-focused learning community and its professional networks in China.

item.title: Decision-Making in the Digital Age: Midbrain Dopaminergic Circuits, Prefrontal Control, and Cognitive Autonomy
item.description: Decision-making is an essential cognitive process for human survival and adaptation, supported by an intricate network that integrates prefrontal executive control, affective processing, and midbrain dopaminergic systems.The digital age has introduced unprecedented environmental pressures, including information overload, persuasive interface design, social validation cues…

item.title: AI as Market Infrastructure: How Misinformation and Automation Inequality Shape Democratic Performance and Economic Wellbeing
item.description: By repositioning AI from firm-level tool to structural infrastructure, the study clarifies how AI-driven market externalities become consequential for consumer welfare, advancing macromarketing theory on emancipation, marketing governance, consumer agency, and public policy in AI-mediated markets.

item.title: Knowledge-Capital Expansion in Modernity: Public Knowledge and Epistemic Capitalization in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
item.description: It treats AI-mediated epistemic capitalization as an historically unfolding transformation whose consequences remain contingent upon changing relations of access, control, attention, experience, circulation, and generativity.

item.title: AI-Assisted Translation Pedagogy for Critical Thinking: A Pathway to Sustainable Education
item.description: The results show that while students frequently use AI for translation, writing, and language learning, their engagement remains primarily functional and efficiency-driven.

item.title: THE INFLUENCE OF DIGITAL DISTRACTION ON UNIVERSITY STUDENTS' ENGLISH LEARNING
item.description: This article examines the influence of digital distraction on university students' English learning through an integrative review of recent international studies and research conducted in the context of Uzbekistan.

item.title: AI-Driven Urge Regulation Assistant (AURA): Designing Preemptive Smart Wearables for Smoking Cessation
item.description: Through an iterative co-design interview process, we examine (1) the barriers and facilitators to smoking cessation and (2) the desired design features of wearable systems targeting cravings before lapses occur.

item.title: THE FUTURE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND ITS APPLICATION AREAS
item.description: This article investigates the current state and foreseeable trajectory of artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on its principal application domains and the governance challenges they raise.

item.title: Digital distraction and self-regulation in distance education
item.description: This study examines the relationship between digital distraction and academic self-regulation among distance education students.

item.title: The Prisoner's Dilemma of AI: Cognitive Offloading Among Future Mathematics Teachers
item.description: This study compares pretest and posttest perceptions of generative AI among first-year pre-service mathematics teachers following a targeted educational intervention focused on principles of AI functioning and related cognitive risks.
